Data dictionary: tables, keys, and relationships

Source: vignettes/data-dictionary.Rmd
data-dictionary.Rmd
library(usaspend)

This is the reference companion to vignette("data-model"): what the package queries at USAspending, what the extract and panel objects contain, which fields drive the accounting, and what the code values mean. Short tables here carry only keys and accounting-critical fields; every table links to its full dictionary as CSV in vignettes/data-dictionary/.

1. The source side: what the package actually queries

It is not one query per table. The package touches four server interfaces, and they map onto the extract’s tables asymmetrically — one bulk-download job returns both prime transactions and subawards; the archives return transactions only; subawards at scale need their own search queries.

# interface what one request covers populates
1 POST /api/v2/download/transactions/ (bulk job) up to ~20 UEIs × a date range → a zip of 4 CSVs: assistance + contract prime transactions, plus FSRS subawards where a queried UEI is the subawardee transactions and subawards (inbound)
2 Award Data Archive files (files.usaspending.gov) one fiscal year × one family, all recipients → filtered locally with duckdb transactions only
3 POST /api/v2/search/spending_by_award/ with subawards = true FSRS lines filtered by prime award_ids (→ outbound) or by recipient_search_text (→ inbound) subawards
4 GET /api/v2/awards/{award_key}/ one prime award’s summary (subaward_count, lifetime totals) the pass-through screen; awards enrichment

Behind those endpoints, USAspending’s warehouse — as far as these queries can see it — looks like this. Two transaction systems (FABS for assistance, FPDS for contracts) hang off a derived award summary; FSRS subaward reports reference a prime award and two recipients:

erDiagram
    RECIPIENT ||--o{ AWARD : "holds (current)"
    AWARD ||--o{ FABS_TRANSACTION : "assistance actions"
    AWARD ||--o{ FPDS_TRANSACTION : "contract actions"
    AWARD ||--o{ FSRS_SUBAWARD : "prime side"
    RECIPIENT ||--o{ FSRS_SUBAWARD : "subawardee side"
    AWARD |o--o{ AWARD : "parent IDV"
    RECIPIENT {
        string uei PK
        string parent_uei FK
        string name
    }
    AWARD {
        string award_key PK "generated_unique_award_id"
        string award_id "FAIN or PIID -- reused, not unique"
        string recipient_uei FK "as of latest action"
        numeric total_obligated "lifetime, recomputed per pull"
    }
    FABS_TRANSACTION {
        string transaction_key PK
        string award_key FK
        date action_date
        numeric federal_action_obligation
        string correction_delete_code
    }
    FPDS_TRANSACTION {
        string transaction_key PK
        string award_key FK
        date action_date
        numeric federal_action_obligation
    }
    FSRS_SUBAWARD {
        string subaward_number "unique per prime only"
        string prime_award_key FK
        string subawardee_uei FK "often null"
        numeric subaward_amount
        date subaward_action_date
    }

Two source facts worth reading off the diagram: award_id (FAIN/PIID) is not unique — agencies reuse it, which is why every join in the package runs on the generated award_key; and an FSRS line has two recipient edges, which is why subaward direction exists only relative to an organization’s UEI set.

2. The extract object — us_extract() / us_sample_extract()

Four elements: two data tables plus the acquisition manifest (jobs) and provenance (meta). The tables are harmonized but not normalized — duplicates, D-flagged deletes, and aggregate records are still present, which is why us_panel() re-normalizes.

erDiagram
    AWARD ||--o{ TRANSACTIONS : "award_key (implicit -- spine built later)"
    AWARD |o--o{ SUBAWARDS : "prime_award_key (inbound rows point OUTSIDE the extract)"
    TRANSACTIONS {
        string transaction_key PK
        string award_key FK
        date action_date
        numeric federal_action_obligation
    }
    SUBAWARDS {
        string subaward_key PK "prime|number|date"
        string prime_award_key FK
        string prime_uei
        string subawardee_uei
        numeric subaward_amount
    }

Note the second edge: for inbound subaward rows the prime award belongs to another organization, so prime_award_key usually matches nothing in your own transactions. That is by design — inbound rows are revenue that prime data cannot see.

$transactions — one row per award action (full dictionary, 48 fields):

field role in the accounting
transaction_key PK; the de-duplication key
award_key FK to the award; every join runs on it
action_date the date money is booked on; years recomputed from it
federal_action_obligation the revenue measure; sign = truth
pragmatic_obligation loan-aware variant (subsidy cost for loans)
loan_face_value / loan_subsidy_cost carried separately; never revenue
award_total_obligated award-lifetime stamp; the reconciliation target
recipient_uei who held the award at this action (can change)
award_group / award_family / award_type_code the include/exclude switches
action_type_code / action_class what kind of action (context only — see §5)
correction_delete_code C kept, D dropped in normalization
record_type_code 1 = aggregate record, dropped
last_modified_date de-duplication tiebreaker; vintage marker

$subawards — one row per FSRS report line (full dictionary, 24 fields):

field role in the accounting
subaward_key PK: prime_award_key \| subaward_number \| action_date; restatement de-dup key
prime_award_key FK to the prime award
prime_uei / subawardee_uei the two sides; direction is computed from them
subaward_amount committed dollars (≥ $30k only; a floor)
subaward_action_date the booking date (report dates lag)
report_last_modified restatement tiebreaker
direction NA until us_normalize_subawards() assigns it

$jobs is the acquisition manifest (download jobs or archive files); $meta records uei, years, source, and subawards — which directions were fetched, so a zero can never pass as a measured zero.

3. The panel object — us_panel()

Five tables plus meta. The panel is keyed org × award × year; organization-level inbound revenue lives in its own table because it cannot sit on another organization’s award rows.

erDiagram
    ORG ||--o{ PANEL : "org_id"
    AWARDS ||--o{ PANEL : "award_key"
    AWARDS ||--o{ TRANSACTIONS : "award_key"
    AWARDS |o--o{ SUBAWARDS : "prime_award_key (outbound)"
    ORG ||--o{ SUBAWARDS_IN : "org_id x year"
    ORG {
        string org_id PK "from us_org_map()"
    }
    AWARDS {
        string award_key PK
        string recipient_uei "as of latest action"
        numeric total_obligated "reconciliation target"
        int n_recipients "gt 1 = PI transfer"
    }
    TRANSACTIONS {
        string transaction_key PK
        string award_key FK
    }
    PANEL {
        string org_id PK
        string award_key PK
        int year PK
        numeric obligation_net
        numeric subaward_out_amount
        numeric net_revenue
    }
    SUBAWARDS {
        string subaward_key PK
        string prime_award_key FK
        string direction
    }
    SUBAWARDS_IN {
        string org_id PK
        int year PK
        numeric subaward_in_amount
    }

$panel — the deliverable (full dictionary, 30 fields):

field role
org_id + award_key + year composite PK (grain asserted by us_audit())
obligation_positive / obligation_negative gross components — never dropped
obligation_net their sum; a commitment, not cash; can be negative
subaward_out_amount pass-through paid onward
net_revenue obligation_net − subaward_out_amount
loan_face_value carried separately, never in net_revenue
award_family the include/exclude switch (loans, student aid)
flags subawards_out_not_fetched ⇒ net_revenue = obligation_net

$awards — the spine (full dictionary, 33 fields): attributes as of the latest action, total_obligated (the reconciliation target), obligated_in_extract (what this window saw), and n_recipients (> 1 flags PI-transfer awards).

$transactions / $subawards — the normalized inputs, same shapes as §2 plus normalization flags (is_zero_dollar, is_deobligation, is_stray_uei, …) and assigned direction.

$subawards_in — org × year inbound revenue (dictionary): subaward_in_amount, n_subawards_in. Folded into totals by us_rollup() as total_net = obligation_net + subaward_in − subaward_out.

4. Code values: award types and families

The full award-type taxonomy, classified live from the package (us_classify_award_type() over every code), with each type’s footprint in the 50-nonprofit pilot. A zero is informative: loan guarantees (08) and insurance (09) exist in the taxonomy but never appear in this population.

codes <- us_classify_award_type(us_award_type_codes())
d <- read.csv("data-dictionary/pilot-descriptives.csv")
n <- aggregate(cbind(actions = n_transactions, awards = n_awards) ~ award_type_code,
               data = d, sum)
tab <- merge(codes, n, by = "award_type_code", all.x = TRUE)
tab[is.na(tab)] <- 0
tab <- tab[order(tab$award_group, tab$award_family, tab$award_type_code),
           c("award_group", "award_family", "award_type_code", "award_type_label",
             "actions", "awards")]
names(tab) <- c("group", "family", "code", "label", "pilot actions", "pilot awards")
tab$`pilot actions` <- format(tab$`pilot actions`, big.mark = ",")
tab$`pilot awards`  <- format(tab$`pilot awards`,  big.mark = ",")
knitr::kable(tab, row.names = FALSE, align = c("l", "l", "l", "l", "r", "r"))

The families are the revenue-treatment switch:

award_family treatment
grant revenue
contract revenue
other revenue-like (cooperative R&D)
direct_payment usually excluded — student aid flowing through the institution
loan obligation is $0 by design; face value never touches revenue
idv a vehicle: obligations only, never ceilings; money is on the delivery orders

5. Code values: action types and classes

Action codes collide across families — the same letter means different things — so classification always takes the family:

knitr::kable(us_classify_action(c("A", "B", "C", "D"), "assistance"))
award_group action_type_code action_type_label action_class
assistance A New origination
assistance B Continuation continuation
assistance C Revision revision
assistance D Adjustment to Completed Award adjustment 
knitr::kable(us_classify_action(c("A", "B", "C", "D", "G", "K", "M"), "contract"))
award_group action_type_code action_type_label action_class
contract A Additional Work (new agreement) origination
contract B Supplemental Agreement Within Scope revision
contract C Funding Only Action funding_only
contract D Change Order revision
contract G Exercise an Option continuation
contract K Close Out closeout
contract M Other Administrative Action administrative

action_class describes intent, never sign: a continuation can carry a negative amount and a termination can carry zero. De-obligations are identified from the amount’s sign alone.

6. Code values: subaward direction

Direction exists only relative to an organization’s UEI set, which is why us_normalize_subawards() requires one:

direction meaning panel treatment
out the org is the prime — pass-through it owes onward subtracted: net_revenue = obligation_net − subaward_out
in the org is the subawardee — revenue invisible in prime data added, in subawards_in (org × year)
internal both sides belong to the org (e.g. NYU → NYU School of Medicine) excluded from both flows
unrelated neither side is the org (multi-recipient award now held elsewhere) excluded

7. The pilot, summarized at this grain

The 50-nonprofit pilot (FY2008–FY2025; 302,025 transactions; outbound pass-through fetched per prime award), by award group, family, and type. Static snapshot computed by data-raw/make-pilot-descriptives.R; also available as CSV.

d <- read.csv("data-dictionary/pilot-descriptives.csv")
## dollars in billions; "\\$" keeps pandoc from pairing the dollar signs
## across cells and reading the span between them as math
usd <- function(x) {
  s <- sprintf("\\$%.2f", abs(x) / 1e9)
  ifelse(x < 0 & round(abs(x) / 1e9, 2) > 0, paste0("-", s), s)
}
short <- c("Direct Payment for Specified Use"     = "Direct Payment (Specified)",
           "Direct Payment with Unrestricted Use" = "Direct Payment (Unrestricted)",
           "Other Financial Assistance"           = "Other Assistance",
           "IDC Indefinite Quantity"              = "IDC (Indef. Qty)",
           "Definitive Contract"                  = "Definitive")
type <- ifelse(d$award_type_label %in% names(short),
               short[d$award_type_label], d$award_type_label)
row <- function(fam, ty, x) data.frame(
  family = fam, type = ty,
  actions = format(x$n_transactions, big.mark = ","),
  awards  = format(x$n_awards, big.mark = ","),
  positive = usd(x$obligation_positive), negative = usd(x$obligation_negative),
  net = usd(x$obligation_net), passthrough = usd(x$subaward_out),
  `net revenue` = usd(x$net_revenue), check.names = FALSE)
tab <- rbind(
  row(d$award_family, type, d),
  row("", "**TOTAL**", as.data.frame(t(colSums(
    d[, c("n_transactions", "n_awards", "obligation_positive", "obligation_negative",
          "obligation_net", "subaward_out", "net_revenue")])))))
knitr::kable(tab, align = c("l", "l", rep("r", 7)))

Dollar figures are billions. The family column implies the award group: grant, direct_payment, loan, and other are assistance awards; contract and idv are contracts. (awards in the TOTAL row slightly overcounts distinct awards, since a few span families.)

The table is the whole accounting argument in one place: project grants and cooperative agreements carry both the dollars and nearly all the pass-through; direct payments are student aid; loans net to zero obligations by design; IDVs hold no money of their own. Total net revenue: $105.9bn on $118.5bn of net obligations.
